what: On a link click, two dark doors close toward the center from both sides of the screen in .8s expo.in as the beam of light in the gap narrows (brightening to .85 then going out at .3s), and the light on the door edges turns on from .3s. The closed doors bounce for .09s and settle, then from .78s the next section name rises letter by letter (.05s apart over .28s, from .25em below) and slides up at .3s as the page moves on. On the next page, the closed doors open after .12s in 1s expo.inOut while a warm light spreads once (up to .72 over .32s → out in .75s)

options.name: Name of the next page to appear on the closed door — if none, the link’s data-name, and if that’s missing, the link text
options.close: Length of door closing (sec), default .8 — 0 moves immediately
options.open: Length of the door opening on the next page (s), default 1
options.wait: Only visitors arriving from the next page within this time (ms) get the door opened, default 5000

use: Receive a quote — Load fx-core.js and this part on the next page too (the door opening runs as soon as the part file loads)
note: The door cover is created once by the part at the end of body (.fx-door). To keep a frame from showing through before the door is drawn on the next page, load this part’s js in head or put it at the start of body. Other windows, new tabs, same-page anchors and modifier-key clicks are not intercepted. Under reduced motion it is covered in .2s and then navigates

from.where: shared.js door transition (original pt-*.js — close .8 xin·light .85 p2in·rim from .3s·.8s bounce .09/.16·letters .78s+.05 gap .28 p2out·exit .3 p2in, open 1s xio after .12s·bleed .22s .32 → .54s .75 p2io)
